note: Rain garden lists read for 0.9.132 (the Rain garden style). wet: entries a list places in the basin or wet bottom; slope: entries for the moist middle, or from a list that gives no zones. Dry-rim, berm and upland entries and genus-only entries are not recorded. Catalog matches are by binomial; plants maps each catalog key to the lists that name it, by continent.
rule: A plant is in RAIN_GARDEN_KEYS (js/ui.js) for a continent where two of that continent's lists name it, or one puts it in the wet bottom and its record says moist soil. A floating water plant never is. A sedge or grass of open, moist ground native to the garden (filed under Wet meadow) earns the rain role in code, without a list.

cautions.lakesedge: MPCA, Plants for Stormwater Design (2024): "Lake sedge is aggressive, so it would probably not be ideal for landscape conditions or rain gardens." https://stormwater.pca.state.mn.us/sites/stormwater/files/Updated%20Plants%20for%20Stormwater%20Design%208.5%20by%2011%2010-25-24%20Low.pdf . The University of Minnesota names it for rain gardens. It is a wet meadow sedge and carries the role as one.
cautions.awlfruitedsedge: MPCA, same guide: well adapted to partially sunny to shaded wet basins, and used in vegetated swales.
cautions.prairiesedge: No rain garden list read names it; Minnesota Wildflowers and Go Botany place it in wet meadows and calcareous fens. It carries the role as a wet meadow sedge, not from a list.

lists.title: City of Madison, Rain Garden Plant List
lists.counted: "Plants for wet soils and rain garden basins" and "medium/mesic soils and rain garden slopes"; not the berm list

lists.title: Brooklyn Botanic Garden, Native Plants for New York City Rain Gardens
lists.counted: sunny wet zone, shady wet zone and wet-zone shrubs; not the uplands
lists.note: Lists Acorus calamus among natives of New York, so read as the native A. americanus

lists.title: Missouri Botanical Garden, RainScaping plant list: Native Plants for Moist to Average Soils
lists.counted: rows marked for the "Rain garden basin (wet)" column; rows marked for slopes only are not counted

lists.title: NC State Extension, Extension Gardener Rain Garden Plant List
lists.counted: every species-level entry (the list gives no zones)

lists.title: Virginia Cooperative Extension 426-043, Rain Garden Plants
lists.counted: every species-level entry (the list gives no zones)

lists.title: University of Minnesota Extension, Rain gardens
lists.counted: entries marked s (saturated) or w (wet); not those marked only um or ud (upland)
lists.note: Prints Acorus calumus; read as the native A. americanus, as above

lists.title: Illinois DNR, Rain Garden Requirements and Plant Lists
lists.counted: "Moist Soil - Full Sun" as the wet placement, "Medium Soil - Full Sun" as the slope

lists.title: Penn State Extension, Rain Garden Resources
lists.counted: Wet/Moist, Moist and Moist/Dry zones ("the workhorses of most rain gardens"); not the Dry zone. Common names only on the page; the species are read from them

lists.title: RHS, Rain gardens
lists.counted: "for the base and inlet" as the wet placement; "tolerate temporarily wet soil as well as dry" as the slope; Hemerocallis is genus-only and not counted

lists.title: RHS, Herbaceous perennials, grasses, ferns and bulbs for seasonally wet and dry soils
lists.counted: every species-level entry; Agapanthus is genus-only and not counted

lists.title: Bray, Gedge, Grant and Leuthvilay, UK Rain Garden Guide (raingardens.info)
lists.counted: the three it says prefer the wetter areas near the inlet as the wet placement; every other species-level entry as the slope; genus-only entries (Aster, Crocosmia, Helenium, Bergenia, Hosta, Allium, Aquilegia) not counted

lists.title: UW-Madison Extension Waukesha County, Rain Garden Species for Full to Part Sun; and for Full to Partial Shade
lists.counted: the clayey-soil lists (plants of wet and emergent habitats) as the wet placement; the silty, sandy and well-drained lists as the slope
lists.note: Lists Acorus calamus with a native wetland habitat, so read as the native A. americanus

lists.title: Nebraska Extension, Proven Rain Garden Plants for Nebraska
lists.counted: every species-level entry, all offered for the wet bottom, which "fills with water for 12 to 48 hours after rainfall"; hardy geranium is named by the cultivar Rozanne
